source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: To examine the effect of different doses of ultrasound on cells, neural responses under different laser burst durations of 4.5, 3, and 1 ms were recorded under the same averaged laser power of 41 mW (Figure 4f–h).
The laser had durations of 4.5 ms (N = 10), 3 ms (N = 20), and 1 ms (N = 10).

A CS-TFOE was positioned within 20 µm above a targeted neuron using a micromanipulator, and it was operated under a 1030 nm laser with 3 ns pulse width at a repetition rate of 3.3 kHz, and a power of 41 mW over a duration of 3 ms.

flags.reason: The 30 MHz central frequency was measured during separate device characterisation (optical detection of the CS-TFOE signal), not necessarily re-measured during the in vitro neuromodulation experiment itself; assumed representative of the same device/laser conditions.

Counts (N=10, N=20, N=10) are per burst-duration condition in the dose-response calcium-imaging experiment; the paper does not state whether these are distinct neurons across conditions or state a combined total, so group sizes are listed rather than summed.

Sham/control here is a 'laser-only' control (bare fibre, no photoacoustic coating) and a 'photothermal-only' control (CW laser, no nanosecond pulsing); closest listed category is inactive_transducer (no ultrasound generated) though the mechanism differs from a conventional TUS sham.

readout_other: Calcium fluorescence imaging (GCaMP6f, ΔF/F0) of cortical neurons
direction_notes: Photoacoustic stimulation via the CS-TFOE produced dose-dependent calcium activation (ΔF/F0 increases) in targeted single neurons; a 3 ms burst produced transient activation (~65% ΔF/F0), a 4.5 ms burst caused overactivation (250% ΔF/F0) with failure to return to baseline, and a 1 ms burst produced no activation.
safety_notes: A 4.5 ms laser burst duration caused overactivation of neurons (250% ΔF/F0) with an inability to return to baseline after 20 s, indicating possible neuronal damage; a 3 ms burst produced transient, reversible activation without apparent damage over the repeated-stimulation test window.

exposures.label: Photoacoustic (CS-TFOE) stimulation of single GCaMP6f-labeled cortical neurons in vitro

target.label: GCaMP6f labelled rat cortical neurons in vitro

device.model: Candle Soot-based Tapered Fiber Optoacoustic Emitter (CS-TFOE)

timing.protocol_description: A CS-TFOE was positioned within 20 µm above a targeted neuron using a micromanipulator, and it was operated under a 1030 nm laser with 3 ns pulse width at a repetition rate of 3.3 kHz, and a power of 41 mW over a duration of 3 ms. Neural responses under different laser burst durations of 4.5, 3, and 1 ms were recorded under the same averaged laser power of 41 mW. Repeated stimulation was performed over the course of two minutes with a time interval of 40 s between trials.
